append.detail: claimFounderRewards decided newlyRewarded and completing from an unlocked read of profiles.meta, stamped the flags through merge_profile_meta (a blind meta || patch that never reports whether the key was already set) and then paid awardGems, so N overlapping claims (two tabs, or parallel posts of the server action) each read rewarded=[] before any stamp landed, each stamped and each paid PER_TASK_GEMS x tasks plus the completion bonus. Replaced the stamp with a compare-and-set: migration 20270345011800 adds claim_founder_flags(p_profile_id, p_tasks, p_complete), service_role only by grant and inside the body, which selects the profile row FOR UPDATE, stamps only the tasks not yet in meta.founder.rewarded (and the badge when p_complete and not yet set) with the same shallow top-level merge, and returns {added, completing}; the action now pays for that returned set only and pays nothing on an RPC error or a malformed answer. Pinned by app/(main)/founder/founder-actions.test.ts (the second tab whose claim returned added=[] pays nothing; bonus only when completing; failed stamp pays nothing; malformed answer claims nothing) and by supabase/tests/claim_founder_flags.test.sql (20 pgTAP assertions: grants, in-body refusal of a non-service caller, second claim of the same tasks returns [], badge completes once, other writers' keys survive, null and malformed founder key tolerated). The SQL was replayed against a throwaway Postgres 16, including a two-session test where the second session blocked on the row lock and came back with added=[]. scripts/function-grants.txt gained the internal verdict for the new function.
